The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto centres on five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills and create jobs. They would replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expand apprenticeships, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The manifesto commits to responsible fiscal management while repairing trade relationships with Europe. Tax proposals include reversing bank tax cuts, increasing the Digital Services Tax, and reforming capital gains tax.

## Health and Social Care

Central pledges include guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and ensuring NHS dental access for emergency care. Mental health provisions include walk-in hubs for young people and professionals in every school. The party proposes free personal care based on the Scottish model, a Royal College of Care Workers, and increased Carer's Allowance with expanded eligibility.

## Education

Proposals include placing mental health professionals in all schools, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. Early years investment would include extra free hours for disadvantaged three and four-year-olds.

## Environment

The manifesto commits to net zero by 2045, with 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home energy upgrade programme would provide free insulation and heat pumps for low-income households. Water companies would be transformed into public benefit companies, with bonuses banned until sewage discharges end. Targets include doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050.

## Housing

The party would build 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities. Renters would receive protection through banned no-fault evictions and three-year default tenancies. Rough sleeping would be ended within the Parliament.

## Crime and Justice

Proposals include restoring community policing, guaranteeing police attendance at all burglaries, and creating an Online Crime Agency. Court backlogs would be addressed through increased investment, with rehabilitation programmes expanded to reduce reoffending.

## Immigration

The party would scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establish safe legal routes for refugees, and process asylum claims within three months. Asylum seekers could work after three months of waiting. Work visa policy would move from the Home Office to relevant departments.

## Democratic Reform

Key reforms include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, scrapping voter ID requirements, and capping political donations. The Ministerial Code would become law, and House of Lords reform would proceed.

## International Affairs

The manifesto prioritises repairing EU relations through a four-stage roadmap, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership. Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP, Army cuts would be reversed, and international development spending would return to 0.7% of national income. The party supports Ukraine and advocates for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza with recognition of Palestinian statehood.

## Families and Welfare

Proposals include extending free school meals to all children in poverty, doubling Statutory Maternity Pay to £350 weekly, and removing the two-child benefit limit. The triple lock on pensions would be maintained, and compensation for 1950s-born women would be delivered.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview

The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and public service decline. It proposes significant public investment funded through wealth taxation and borrowing.

## Health and Social Care

The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

For social care, the manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment, free personal care, improved pay and career structures for carers, and increased disability benefits by 5%.

## Housing

The manifesto targets 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering local authorities to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A £29bn five-year programme would retrofit homes for energy efficiency, with additional funding for heating systems and climate adaptation.

## Energy and Environment

The party proposes wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, no new oil and gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and community ownership of energy sources. Nuclear power development would cease. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would rise to £500 within ten years.

Environmental commitments include a Rights of Nature Act, 30% of land and seas protected by 2030, water companies returned to public ownership, and £1.5bn additional DEFRA funding.

## Economy and Work

The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. A £15 minimum wage for all ages, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, and restored trade union rights are proposed. Anti-union legislation since 1979 would be repealed.

## Welfare and Cost of Living

Proposals include increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, ending the five-week benefit wait, abolishing the two-child cap, increasing carer's allowance by 10%, and scrapping the bedroom tax.

## Education

The manifesto proposes £8bn school investment including teacher pay increases, £2.5bn annually for building repairs, £5bn for special needs provision, free school meals for all children, scrapping tuition fees, and restoring maintenance grants.

## Transport

Proposals include £10bn annual public transport subsidies, railways returned to public ownership, free bus travel for under-18s, £2.5bn annually for cycleways and footpaths, ending new petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027, and opposing new road building.

## Democracy and Rights

The manifesto proposes replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, defending the Human Rights Act, and repealing recent protest restriction legislation.

## Immigration

Proposals include ending the hostile environment policy, removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during applications, and ending immigration detention except for public safety cases.

## International Affairs

The manifesto calls for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, restoring overseas aid to 0.7% of GNI rising to 1%, and rejoining the EU. On defence, it proposes signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and cancelling Trident, while remaining in NATO with reforms.

## Funding

Revenue would come from wealth taxes on assets above £10m, aligning capital gains and investment income tax rates with employment income, and carbon taxation. The party estimates raising £50-70bn annually from personal taxation reforms and up to £80bn from carbon taxes by parliament's end. Significant borrowing for investment is proposed, with inflation as the primary fiscal constraint rather than conventional debt rules.
